title: Rock Paper Scissors
story: Rock crushes scissors. Scissors cut paper. Paper covers rock. Three choices, nine possible outcomes, centuries of playground dispute resolution. Build the game that pits human strategy against computer randomness — first to 3 wins takes the match.
why: Rock Paper Scissors combines enums for choices, match for determining winners, random selection for AI, and score tracking — a complete two-player game.
analogy: Three warriors in a circular duel: Rock smashes Scissors, Scissors shreds Paper, Paper smothers Rock. Every choice beats one and loses to one — perfect balance, no dominant strategy. Your match loop is the arena where these warriors endlessly clash.
try_it: Track win/loss/draw counts over 100 random games. Add 'Lizard' and 'Spock' (Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock — 5 choices, 25 outcomes). Implement a 'strategy' computer that always plays the move that would beat the player's most common previous move.
tips: Only 3 winning conditions because draw is handled first
Use enums for choices and results — much clearer than strings
Random computer choice makes games unpredictable and fair
common_mistakes: Forgetting to check for draw first — otherwise you might misclassify
Having 6 conditions (2 per choice) when 3 is enough (check win only, else lose)
Hardcoding player choices — a real game would read input or simulate random play
